whyItMatters: Only 6.0% of free trials become paying teams, yet the funnel shows exactly where the value is lost: 54% create a first project, but just 29% ever invite a teammate and only 22% reach a shared board. The product is a team tool used, at first, by one person migrating off spreadsheets or Trello — so it stays quiet in week one and never earns the second project. The most striking signal is behavioural, not attitudinal: trials that invite a teammate within 48 hours convert at 19% versus 3% otherwise. Fixing conversion is therefore less about persuasion and more about getting the team into the workspace before the trial goes cold. Naming that as the measurable target keeps later phases focused on the few behaviours that move paid conversion rather than on discounting.
objective: More trial teams reach a genuinely shared workspace in week one — a teammate invited and a shared board created early — so that trial-to-paid conversion rises without discounting.

keyResults.kr: Increase the share of trials that create a shared board (activation) in week one
Increase the share of trials that invite a teammate within the first 48 hours
keyResults.baseline: 29% of signups invite at all; invite-within-48h not separately tracked
keyResults.target: Grow the within-48h invite share (set once instrumented)

keyResults.kr: Lift trial-to-paid conversion from its current baseline

gapLog.content: Week-one 'quiet' is reported by Sales but not instrumented — there is no in-product engagement measure for the first seven days.
The 19%-vs-3% invite/no-invite conversion gap is treated as directional, not proven causal; a teammate invite may be a marker of already-committed teams.
Confirm which team owns the 7-step workspace-setup wizard, since fixing it spans Product and Support.
Invite-within-48h is not separately tracked today, so KR2's target cannot be set until the metric exists.
